security_audit.summary: All 28 external-command alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences or JavaScript template literals. The reconnaissance alert is also false, but sending development content to Copilot and enabling all tools create two contextual medium risks.

remediation.issue: The implementation example enables all Copilot tools without explaining the resulting permission scope.
remediation.suggestion: Default allowAllTools to false and require explicit user approval before granting broader tool access.

remediation.issue: Prompts, source code, errors, and context can be sent to GitHub Copilot.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear data-sharing warning and advise users to remove secrets, credentials, and restricted code before submission.

content.user_title: Use GitHub Copilot MCP Tools for Development
content.value_statement: Development tasks often require separate prompts for review, debugging, testing, and explanation. This skill connects Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to focused GitHub Copilot MCP tools.
actual_capabilities: Ask GitHub Copilot general development questions with optional context and model selection.
Submit code for reviews focused on security, performance, maintainability, or best practices.
Request code explanations or debugging analysis with error and context details.
Receive refactoring suggestions aligned with a stated improvement goal.
Generate unit test suggestions for a selected testing framework.
Start sessions and retrieve conversation history for related development tasks.
limitations: An active GitHub Copilot subscription, CLI authentication, and MCP server configuration are required.
Prompts and code are processed by GitHub Copilot, so sensitive content requires careful handling.
Available models and usage limits depend on the connected Copilot plan and current service configuration.
Generated reviews, commands, and code require human validation before execution or deployment.

use_cases.title: Review a pull request
use_cases.description: Inspect changed code for security, performance, maintainability, and best-practice concerns before approval.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a failing feature
use_cases.description: Analyze relevant code, the observed error, and execution context to identify likely causes and fixes.

use_cases.title: Build focused unit tests
use_cases.description: Generate test cases for an existing function using the project testing framework and expected behaviors.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a function
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this code in simple terms, including its inputs, outputs, and main control flow: {code}

prompt_templates.title: Debug an error
prompt_templates.prompt: Debug this code using the error and context. Identify the likely cause and propose a verified fix: {code} {error} {context}

prompt_templates.title: Generate unit tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate unit test cases for this code using {framework}. Cover normal behavior, edge cases, and expected failures: {code}

prompt_templates.title: Review an architecture change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed change for security, performance, maintainability, and migration risk. Rank findings and explain tradeoffs: {proposal} {context}

output_examples.input: Explain a function that validates and normalizes an email address.
output_examples.output: The function validates the input format, normalizes casing where appropriate, and returns either a canonical address or a validation error.

output_examples.input: Review an authentication query for security and maintainability.
output: High priority: Replace interpolated query values with parameterized statements.
High priority: Store and compare password hashes instead of plaintext passwords.
Medium priority: Return a generic authentication error to reduce account discovery.

output_examples.input: Debug a response parser that reports a missing JSON function.
output_examples.output: The parser references the method without calling it. Invoke the response method, await its result, and add handling for invalid response bodies.

best_practices: Provide the smallest relevant code sample, exact error, expected behavior, and runtime context.
Choose focused review areas and a model appropriate for the task complexity.
Remove secrets and restricted code before sending content to Copilot.
anti_patterns: Do not grant all tools unless the task requires them and the user approves the expanded access.
Do not combine unrelated tasks in one session because previous context can reduce answer relevance.
Do not execute generated commands or deploy generated code without review and testing.

faq.question: What is required to use this skill?
faq.answer: You need an active GitHub Copilot subscription, authenticated Copilot CLI access, and a configured MCP client.

faq.question: Which development tasks are supported?
faq.answer: The documented tools cover general questions, reviews, explanations, debugging, refactoring, test generation, command suggestions, and session management.

faq.question: Can I choose a Copilot model?
faq.answer: Yes. Several tools accept a model name, but availability depends on your plan and current Copilot configuration.

faq.question: Does the skill keep conversation context?
faq.answer: Yes. Session tools can start a conversation and retrieve its history for related follow-up tasks.

faq.question: Is my source code sent to an external service?
faq.answer: Yes. Submitted prompts, code, errors, and context are processed through GitHub Copilot. Remove sensitive material before use.

faq.question: Should I enable all Copilot tools?
faq.answer: Enable all tools only when necessary and after reviewing the connected permissions. Use narrower access for routine tasks.
